findings.problem: The ALLegs namespace contains a nontrivial extensionality lemma. It proves by adjoin_induction (mem, algebraMap via ratCast, add, inv, mul) that two ring homs out of modularFunctionFieldFull N are equal once they agree on the generators qExpand ℚ e jq. A sibling solution file has the identical lemma, with the same name and the same proof. The sibling is P2M/Sol/S_ModularCurve_coe_atkinLehnerInvolutionFull_mul_eq_qExpand_of_coe_eq_qExpand.lean, lines 22-46. The generic ringHom_ext_full proof is therefore maintained twice, and a change to the definition of modularFunctionFieldFull would require edits in both files. The file also contains a second, shorter duplicate, dvd_mul_prime_cases. It is copied verbatim into the sibling file at lines 15-20. Two other files (heckeAlphaBar and heckeBetaBar) carry private variants with a different proof but the same statement without the ¬ q ∣ N₀ hypothesis.
findings.proposed_change: Move ringHom_ext_full into the Definitions or Theorems module that defines modularFunctionFieldFull and jqd_mem_full. Its statement is unchanged: `{g₁ g₂ : ↥(modularFunctionFieldFull N) →+* L} (h : ∀ e [NeZero e] (he : e ∣ N), g₁ ⟨qExpand ℚ e jq, jqd_mem_full N he⟩ = g₂ ⟨qExpand ℚ e jq, jqd_mem_full N he⟩) : g₁ = g₂`. Its proof is also unchanged: adjoin_induction with the mem, algebraMap, add, inv and mul cases. Move the divisor-splitting lemma next to it. The version in the heckeAlphaBar and heckeBetaBar files drops the unused `hqN : ¬ q ∣ N₀` hypothesis and could be the shared one. Then delete the local `namespace ALLegs` block (lines 13-48). Both Atkin-Lehner solutions would call `ringHom_ext_full` directly with their existing `apply ringHom_ext_full; intro e _ he`. The `private` copies in the hecke files would use the shared lemma. The imports already cover both solutions, because the target imports Definitions.Def_ModularCurve_AtkinLehnerPartial. A shared lemma needs an import chain from that module or an earlier one.
findings.benefit: The adjoin_induction argument and the divisor split exist once instead of four times. Edits to the field definition or to the generator set touch one proof. Each solution file then contains only its own Atkin-Lehner argument.
